main_text.head: CAPUT XLIII.
main_text.p: Bilis fla-va.Flava bilis seu cholera est humor secundi generis, substantiâ tenuis, δυνάμει calidus & siccus, sapore amarus, colore flavus, ex tenuioribus & calidioribus ehyli[?] partibus enatus, qui secretus in fellis vesicam recedit, & exemtus venis, non coagulatur.

Hæc bilis est vel alimentaria, vel non alimentaria. Alimentaria est massæ sanguineæ pars tenuissima, per venas distributa, alens particulas suæ naturæ affines, & sanguini per venas perlabenti transvectionis promtitudinem afferens.
Non alimentaria à sanguine secernitur, & in vesiculâ fellis amandatur, proprio deinde ductu in intestina labens.
Vesicula fellis est oblongum & membraneum receptaculum flavæ bilis à sanguine separatæ, sub jecoris parte dextrâ & concavâ situm.
Meatus habet hæc duos: alterum ab Epate, per quem bilis influit in vesiculam: alterum, qui à vesicula porrigitur, in initium intestini Jejuni insertus.
Hujus in intestinis usus est, ad excrementorum dejectionem intestina stimulare (unde & flavo apparent colore)

page.notes: Right margin notes: "Bilis fla-va." beside the first paragraph and "Fellis Ve-sicula" beside the paragraph on the gall bladder. Printed with a hyphen at the line break. The Greek word δυνάμει is read from a small, slightly blurred print and should be checked. "ehyli" is printed as shown, possibly for "chyli"; it is marked [?]. The text ends with the catchword "dein-" at the foot.
